 Judgment

1. Captioned appeal is filed against the impugned judgment and award dated 21.06.2007 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux), Rajkot in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.1708 of 1998, whereby the learned Tribunal had partly allowed the claim petition and awarded a sum of Babubhai Arjanbhai Kalaria vs Nakubhai Valabhai Meghani on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54751016/
1 Rs.2,30,024/- as a compensation along with the interest at the rate of 7.5% per NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1718/2010 JUDGMENT DATED: 01/04/2026 undefined annum from the date of filing of the claim petition till its realization.
2. The succinct facts leading to file the captioned appeal are that on 10.01.1998, at about 01:30 hours, Babubhai Arjanbhai Kalaria was going in the tractor of opponent No.1 as a labourer for loading the stones in the tractor.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claim Petition No.1708 of 1998
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

entities.text: Babubhai Arjanbhai Kalaria vs Nakubhai Valabhai Meghani
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: When he reached at the outskirts of Village- Zinzuda, as there was slope on the road, he got off from the said tractor and was passing on the left side and ahead of the tractor, in the meantime, the driver of the tractor came by driving the said tractor in a rash and negligent manner at very excessive speed so as to endanger the human life and dashed with Babubhai Arjanbhai Kalaria.
As a result of the accident, Babubhai Arjanbhai Kalaria sustained grievous injuries.

2.1. Having been served with the notice of claim petition, the opponent No.2-Insurance Company appeared through its advocate and filed Written Statement, thereby denying the contents of the claim petition and prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.

2.2. Having considered the pleadings of the parties, the learned NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1718/2010 JUDGMENT DATED: 01/04/2026 undefined Tribunal framed the following issues at Exhibit-30, for determination.

"1. Whether the applicant proves that he/she was injured by rash and/or negligent act or the driver of vehicle involved in the accident?
2. Whether the applicant is entitled to recover compensation from the opponents or any of them?
If yes, what amount?

3. What order?"
2.3.

Having considered the oral as well as documentary evidence on record and the submissions canvassed by learned advocates for the parties, the learned Tribunal had awarded a sum of Rs.2,30,024/- as a compensation along with the interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition till realization.
2.4. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award, the appellant-herein preferred the captioned appeal on the ground of quantum.

3. Heard learned advocates for the parties.
4.

Mr. D. D. Bhatt, learned advocate appearing on behalf of the original claimant/appellant,
vehemently submitted that owing to the injuries sustained in the accident, the claimant/appellant has become 100% disable for doing the work,
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1718/2010 JUDGMENT DATED: 01/04/2026 undefined therefore, the learned Tribunal ought to have considered the functional disability at 100%.

He further submitted that the learned Tribunal had assessed the Babubhai Arjanbhai Kalaria vs Nakubhai Valabhai Meghani on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54751016/
2 income of the appellant at a lower side.

entities.text: Babubhai Arjanbhai Kalaria vs Nakubhai Valabhai Meghani
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further submitted that at the time of accident, the appellant was serving as a daily wager in Forest Department and thereby earning a sum of Rs.58.10/- per day.
He further submitted that apart from the daily wager work, the appellant was engaged in agricultural work and thereby earning a sum of Rs.1,000/- per month.

Therefore, the learned Tribunal ought to have considered the income from both the sources, however, the learned Tribunal has assessed the income of the appellant as Rs.1800/- per month which is at a lower side.
He further submitted that the learned Tribunal has awarded a meagre amount of compensation under the head of pain, shock and suffering.

He further submitted that considering the injuries sustained by the appellant in the accident, the learned Tribunal ought to have awarded a sum of Rs.50,000/- under the head of pain, shock and suffering.

4.1. Learned advocate for the appellant further submitted that the learned Tribunal had not awarded any amount of compensation under the head of loss of amenities and loss of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1718/2010 JUDGMENT DATED: 01/04/2026 undefined married life though, the appellant has been deprived of leading a normal marital life owing to the injuries sustained in the vehicular accident.

He further submitted that the learned Tribunal had awarded a meagre amount of compensation under the head of medical expenses, special diet, attendant charges and transportation, actual loss of income.
Therefore, he prayed for enhancement of the compensation.

5. On the other hand, Ms. Krupali N. Bhatt, learned advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No.2-Insurance Company, vehemently submitted that the appellant could not prove the income on record, therefore, the learned Tribunal had rightly considered the income of the appellant as Rs.1800/- per month.
She further submitted that at the time of accident, the minimum wages for the skilled worker was of Rs.1700/-.
Therefore, the learned Tribunal had rightly assessed the income of the appellant at Rs.1800/- from both the sources of income.
She further submitted that the learned Tribunal has awarded the just compensation under all the heads.
She further submitted that there is no infirmity in the impugned judgment and award, therefore, the captioned appeal is liable to be dismissed.

6. Having considered the submissions of the learned NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1718/2010 JUDGMENT DATED: 01/04/2026 undefined advocates for the parties and having gone through the record, the original claimant/appellant-herein has challenged the impugned judgment and award on the ground of quantum.
It is the case of the appellant that at the time of accident, the appellant was working as a daily wager in the Forest Department, and thereby, earning a sum of Rs.58.10/- per day.
Apart from the daily wager, he was also engaged in agricultural work and thereby earning a sum of Rs.1000/- per month.
Considering the evidence on record, the learned Tribunal has assessed the income of the appellant as Rs.1800/- per month.
Perusal of the record transpires that the appellant has not led any cogent evidence to prove his income.
Therefore, in absence of any cogent evidence of income, the learned Tribunal ought to have considered the minimum wages prevalent at the time of accident.
The accident in question occurred on 10.01.1998.
At the relevant point of time, the minimum wages for the skilled worker was of Rs.1700/-.
Therefore, the learned Tribunal has rightly determined the income of the appellant as Rs.1800/- per month.

It is on record that at the time of accident, the appellant was aged about 28 years, therefore, in view of the ratio laid down NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1718/2010 JUDGMENT DATED:
01/04/2026 undefined by the Hon'ble Supreme Court rendered in the case of Sarla Verma & Ors Vs.
Delhi Transport Corp. & Anr. reported in 2009 (06) SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Ltd.
Vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors., reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, 40% of the monthly income is to be added on account of future prospective income of the original claimant/appellant-herein.

sentences.text:
Thus, after adding 40% to the monthly income, it would come to Rs.2520/- (1800 + 40% of 1800).
8.
With the consent of both the parties, the learned Tribunal had assessed the functional disability at 42%.
The appellant has sustained the fracture of pelvis with radius lower end right with rupture urethra.

The appellant has not proved the disability on record by examining the doctor, who issued the disability certificate, however, the appellant and the Insurance Company before the learned Tribunal agreed to consider the disability at 42% body as a whole.

Thus, considering the functional disability at 42% and applying the multiplier of 17 as per age of the appellant, the future loss of income would come to Rs.2,15,913/- (2520 x 42% x 12 x 17).
9.
The learned Tribunal had awarded a sum of Rs.30,000/- under the head of pain, shock and suffering.

It is evident from NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1718/2010 JUDGMENT DATED:
01/04/2026 undefined
the record that the appellant has sustained multiple fracture and he underwent operation for the same.
He was treated for a long time and he remained hospitalized as an indoor patient for a considerable time.

Thus, considering the facts and circumstances of the present case, the compensation awarded under this head is enhanced from Rs.30,000/- to Rs.50,000/-.
10.
The learned Tribunal had awarded a sum of Rs.25000/- under the head of medical expenses.

It is evident from the record that the appellant had received the treatment in the Madhuram Hospital,
Rajkot as well as from Dr. Jayesh Mehta.

The bill of Madhuram Hospital was considered by the learned Tribunal while awarding the compensation under the head of medical expenses, however,
the treatment taken by the appellant at the Hospital of Dr. Jayesh Mehta was not considered.

He was surgically operated in the Hospital of Dr. Jayesh Mehta, therefore, considering the totality of the facts and circumstances and nature of treatment received by the original claimant/
appellant-herein, the compensation awarded under this head is enhanced from Rs.25000/- to Rs.1,00,000/-.
11. The learned Tribunal had awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/- under the head of special diet, attendant charges and NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1718/2010 JUDGMENT DATED: 01/04/2026 undefined transportation.

Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the original claimant/appellant-herein, the treatment received by the appellant and period of treatment, the compensation awarded under this head is enhanced from Rs.10,000/- to Rs.15,000/-.
12.
The learned Tribunal had awarded a sum of Rs.10,800/- under the head of actual loss of income.

The learned Tribunal had awarded the just compensation under the head of actual loss of income,
therefore, no interference is required under this head.

4 13.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is evident from the record that the appellant has been deprived of leading a normal marital life owing to the injuries sustained in the accident, as he has become impotent.
However, the learned Tribunal had not awarded any amount of compensation under the head of loss of amenities and loss of married life.
Therefore, a sum of Rs.50,000/- is awarded under the head of loss of amenities and loss of married life.

14. Thus, in view of the above discussions, the original claimant/appellant shall be entitled for the following amount of compensation under the following heads:-
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1718/2010 JUDGMENT DATED: 01/04/2026 undefined Particulars Amount (Rs.) Future Loss of Income 2,15,913/-
 Actual Loss of Income   Medical Expenses   Special Diet, Attendant Charges and   Transportation  Pain, Shock and Suffering   Loss of Amenities and Loss of Married Life   Total Compensation   Less: compensation
already awarded by the   learned Tribunal
Additional amount of Compensation  15.
In view of the above discussions, the claimant/appellant shall be entitled for the total compensation of Rs.4,41,713/-.

The learned Tribunal had already awarded a sum of Rs.2,30,024/-, therefore, the claimant/appellant shall be entitled for the additional compensation of Rs.2,11,689/- i. e. (Rs.4,41,713/- -
(less) Rs.2,30,024/-).

The learned Tribunal has awarded the interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum,
therefore, the claimant/appellant shall also be entitled for the interest at the rate of 7.5% on the additional amount of compensation.
16. In view of the above discussions, the captioned appeal stands allowed partly.
The impugned judgment and award is modified to the aforesaid extent.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1718/2010 JUDGMENT DATED: 01/04/2026 undefined 17.

The respondent No.2-Insurance Company is directed to deposit the additional amount of compensation along with the interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition till its realization, within a period of 6 weeks from today.
18. Upon depositing of the said amount, the learned Tribunal shall disburse the amount to the original claimant/s, after deducting the deficit court fees, if any, and after due verification.
